title: Central bank divergence deepens as RBI drains liquidity and BoJ tightens to multi-decade highs
changed: Global monetary policy divergence widened this week as the Bank of Japan raised its policy rate to a 31-year high, increasing the risk of yen carry trade unwinds and cross-border capital repatriation. In Europe, sticky consumer inflation expectations and wage growth tracking at 2.7% reinforced the European Central Bank's measured pace of rate reductions. The Bank of England held its benchmark rate at 3.75% while pausing gilt sales, balancing softer 3.9% wage growth against petrol-driven headline inflation, with all major central banks awaiting the Federal Reserve's dot plot projections.

Energy markets absorbed rising geopolitical tail risks, with Middle East friction threatening upward price moves in Brent crude toward $100 to $120. While Cheniere's completed Corpus Christi LNG expansion added supply capacity to global gas markets, firm refining crack spreads kept downstream transport fuel costs elevated globally. In parallel, US federal opposition to AI development restrictions secured an open runway for mega-cap technology capital expenditure, overcoming safety pause proposals from private lab leadership.

In India, the Reserve Bank shifted its balance sheet stance by detailing a ₹1 lakh crore Open Market Operation (OMO) bond sale across three tranches and executing a ₹25,000 crore auction. Alongside overnight variable rate reverse repo absorptions reaching up to ₹2.4 lakh crore, this permanent liquidity withdrawal anchored overnight money market rates near 4.9%. The absorption pushed primary yields higher, holding the benchmark 2033 G-sec at 6.82% and extending 2041 and 2076 paper cut-offs to 7.23% and 7.69% respectively.

On India's external and regulatory accounts, the July current account deficit widened to $7.0 billion, heightening your reliance on service trade receipts from software exports to buffer the rupee. For your audit and compliance workflow, the RBI rationalised foreign exchange circular frameworks under FEMA, issued draft KYC standard operating procedures for money mule accounts, and adjusted Priority Sector Lending classification rules governing bank balance sheet targets.

threads.name: Sovereign yield curve repricing
threads.note: The RBI's ₹1 lakh crore OMO sale program and state borrowing of ₹16,750 crore have anchored the 10-year G-sec at 6.82% and ultra-long paper at 7.69%. Execution of the remaining OMO tranches and weekly ₹24,000 crore T-bill cut-offs will confirm if long-end yields rise further.

threads.name: Global central bank divergence
threads.note: The BoJ's hike to a 31-year high tightens global liquidity while the BoE holds at 3.75% and the ECB slows rate cuts. Fed dot plot projections will confirm whether widening interest rate differentials accelerate capital repatriation out of emerging assets.

threads.name: Energy cost transmission to twin deficits
threads.note: Brent crude tail risks toward $100 to $120 threaten to expand India's current account deficit beyond the $7.0 billion July print. Stable domestic fuel pricing depends on whether refined product crack spreads soften or global crude shocks materialize.

threads.name: Bank regulatory and balance sheet compliance
threads.note: RBI updates to Priority Sector Lending rules and mandatory SOPs for money mule accounts require adjustments to commercial bank lending targets and internal audits. The transition to SEBI Demat 2.0 tokenised bonds outlines a structural change for corporate debt settlements.
